explain.say: Imagine you walk to school and a friend times you. Every second, you cover 2 metres. Let us turn your walk into a picture called a distance–time graph.

marks.label: 5 s: 10 m

marks.label: 20 s: 40 m
marks.ask: How do you find speed from a distance–time graph?

explain.say: Look at the bottom line. That is time, in seconds. The side line is distance, in metres. See the yellow dot? Go up from 5 seconds, then across: you have walked 10 metres. Can you find where you are at 10 seconds?

marks.label: 5 s: 10 m
marks.ask: How do you read a point on the graph?

marks.label: 20 s: 40 m
marks.ask: How do you find speed from a distance–time graph?

explain.say: Yes, 20 metres! See how the line is perfectly straight? Straight means steady speed: the same distance every second. Speed is distance divided by time, so 20 metres in 10 seconds is 2 metres per second.

marks.label: 5 s: 10 m

marks.label: 20 s: 40 m
marks.ask: How do you find speed from a distance–time graph?

explain.say: The slope tells you the speed. Slope just means how steep the line is. Steeper means more metres each second, so faster. A flat line would mean you stopped. Which line would be steeper, you walking or you cycling?

marks.ask: How do you find speed from a distance–time graph?

explain.say: Cycling, well done! At 20 seconds you are at 40 metres, still 2 metres per second. Wow fact: a sprinting cheetah, about 30 metres per second, would draw a line 15 times steeper than yours. Try sketching your own walk home tomorrow.

faq.q: How do you read a point on the graph?
faq.a: Start at a time on the bottom axis, go straight up to the line, then straight across to the distance axis. That is how far you had gone at that moment.
asks: How do I read a distance-time graph?

faq.q: How do you find speed from a distance–time graph?
faq.a: Pick two points on the line. Divide the distance gained by the time taken. That is the gradient, or slope, and it equals the speed.
asks: What does the gradient of a distance-time graph show?

faq.q: What does a flat line mean on a distance–time graph?
faq.a: A flat line means the distance is not changing, so the object is standing still.
asks: horizontal line on a distance time graph

faq.q: What does a curved line mean?
faq.a: A curve means the speed is changing. If it gets steeper the object is speeding up; if it flattens out it is slowing down.
Because you walk the same distance every second. Equal steps in time give equal steps in distance, so the points sit on a straight line.
asks: What does a straight line mean on the graph?

facts: On a distance–time graph, the gradient (slope) equals the speed.
A cheetah can sprint at roughly 30 metres per second (over 100 km/h) for short bursts.

quiz.say: On a distance–time graph, what does a flat line show?
quiz.show: On a distance–time graph, what does a flat line show?
quiz.why: The distance does not change as time passes, so the object is not moving.

wrong.0: Fast motion gives a steep line, not a flat one.
wrong.2: Speeding up gives a curve that gets steeper.

quiz.say: You walk 60 m in 30 s at a steady speed. What is your speed?
quiz.show: You walk 60 m in 30 s at a steady speed. What is your speed?
quiz.why: Speed = distance ÷ time = 60 ÷ 30 = 2 metres per second.

wrong.0: That subtracts the numbers; speed is distance divided by time.
wrong.1: That multiplies distance by time instead of dividing.
